narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 38% chance that you would become a bad credit risk. Although that is below 50%, it was above the bank’s approval cutoff for this application, so the loan was not approved. The decision was shaped most strongly by three factors. The largest influence was the amount you requested: at 2,579 DM, it was below the approved-applicant average of about 3,020 DM, and this worked in your favor by lowering the estimated risk. The second-largest influence was the 12-month repayment period, which is shorter than the approved average of about 19 months and also reduced the risk estimate. The third-largest influence, and the main unfavorable signal among these top factors, was the condition of your checking account: being below zero DM is much less common among approved applicants (about 12.6%) than having no overdraft (about 59.2%), so this pushed the estimate toward bad credit. Those favorable points were not enough to offset this and other risk indicators in your profile. Next, ask the lender for the specific reasons recorded for the denial and review your checking-account status and credit report for errors or overdue balances. Providing proof of stable income and employment, adding a guarantor or co-applicant, or reapplying after improving your account balance and employment history may strengthen a future application.
